title: GST Appeals, Revision, Advance Ruling and Writ Jurisdiction

content.overview: A GST adjudication order can be appealed to the Appellate Authority, then to the Appellate Tribunal, on the conditions and pre-deposit the Act requires. Revision is a separate departmental power. Advance ruling is a pre-transaction ruling by the Authority for Advance Ruling, not an appeal. A writ is a constitutional remedy, not a GST appellate stage. The forum follows the order being challenged. An advance ruling is not used to reopen an adjudication.
content.glance: GST Appeals, Revision, Advance Ruling and Writ Jurisdiction. Complete Tax treatise with statutory deconstruction, examples, verified authorities, forum analysis and chamber drafting.
content.study: Identify the order, the forum and the pre-deposit. Do not skip the appellate stage by describing a writ as the ordinary remedy.

cases.name: Govind Saran Ganga Saran v. Commissioner of Sales Tax
cases.facts: The Court examined the components of a valid charging provision.
cases.issue: What must a tax levy clearly identify to be valid?
cases.ratioDecidendi: A valid levy ordinarily identifies the taxable event, person liable, rate and measure or value of the tax.
cases.holding: The Court treated these components as essential to a charging scheme.
cases.relevance: Use for charge, levy and statutory certainty.

cases.name: Union of India v. Azadi Bachao Andolan
cases.facts: The Court considered treaty benefits, circulars and tax avoidance arguments.
cases.issue: How should a valid tax treaty and administrative circular operate?
cases.ratioDecidendi: A treaty and valid administrative practice must be respected unless displaced by law; legitimate tax planning is not automatically evasion.
cases.holding: The Court upheld the challenged treaty approach in the circumstances.
cases.relevance: Use for statutory interpretation, treaties and tax planning.

cases.name: Union of India v. Mohit Minerals Pvt. Ltd.
cases.facts: The case concerned GST levy and the legal effect of a Council recommendation.
cases.issue: What is the constitutional and statutory force of GST Council recommendations?
cases.ratioDecidendi: GST Council recommendations have persuasive value within the constitutional design but are not automatically binding as primary legislation without statutory implementation.
cases.holding: The Court interpreted the federal GST framework accordingly.
cases.relevance: Use for GST levy, delegated action and constitutional federalism.

II. GOVERNING RULE
GST Appeals, Revision, Advance Ruling and Writ Jurisdiction is governed by Income-tax Act, 2025; Income-tax Rules, 2026; CGST Act, 2017; IGST Act, 2017; applicable SGST Acts; and Customs Act, 1962, together with current rules, notifications and circulars. identify the tax period, charging statute, commencement date, amendment or notification in force, taxable event, jurisdictional notice and statutory appeal or writ route; use the Income-tax Act, 1961 only as historical transition/concordance where the 2025 Act applies.

III. INGREDIENT APPLICATION
Identify each condition, connect it to the evidence and answer the principal exception or defence. Apply BSA s. 63 to digital records where relevant and state the initial burden precisely.

IV. CONCLUSION
Grant, refuse or modify the relief only to the extent authorised by the governing law and proved record.

enhancement.legalPrinciple: The forum follows the order being challenged. An advance ruling is not used to reopen an adjudication.
essentialIngredients: Tribunal stage after the appellate order
Advance ruling on a stated question
Writ only as a constitutional remedy
enhancement.detailedExplanation: Section 107 is the first appeal and requires a pre-deposit of the admitted amount and a percentage of the disputed tax, as enacted. Section 112 is the Tribunal appeal and has its own pre-deposit. Revision allows the revisional authority to examine an order that is erroneous and prejudicial to revenue. Advance ruling answers classification, liability and similar questions for a proposed transaction. The percentages are statutory and should be read from the current text.
examples: An adjudication order is appealed with the admitted tax paid.
A person asks whether a proposed supply is goods or services.
That is an advance-ruling question, not an appeal.
